kept_items.author: OpenAI
kept_items.text: Introducing a limited preview of GPT-5.6 Sol, our next generation frontier model, as well as GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-5.6 Luna.
kept_items.selection_reason: Top news of the day: OpenAI GPT-5.6 family launch (Sol, Terra, Luna). Thread head, 34.5k likes. Replies unavailable for thread head; using 0, gap noted.

kept_items.author: sama
kept_items.text: Good news: Sol is a smart, efficient step forward. Bad news: at the request of the US government, it launches today in limited preview instead of the open access launch we were planning.
kept_items.selection_reason: Altman's detailed statement on the limited-preview decision and government access process. Distinct company-framing angle. 13.8k likes. Replies unavailable for thread head; using 0, gap noted.

kept_items.author: sama
kept_items.text: actually i think a required preview period for extended redteaming is not a bad idea. i just dont like the idea of the government picking the customers.
kept_items.selection_reason: Altman's sharper distinction during the Q&A: supports a mandated red-team preview window but objects to government choosing customers. Second sama item within cap, distinct policy angle.

kept_items.author: AndrewCurran_
kept_items.text: Semafor reports the US government has lifted its block on Mythos 5 in a letter from Commerce Secretary Lutnick to Tom Brown. Fable not included. US only, 100 US institutions.
kept_items.selection_reason: Concrete policy counterpart: Commerce lifts export block on Anthropic's Mythos 5 for 100 US institutions, Fable excluded. Factual report citing Semafor, 133k views.

kept_items.author: AnthropicAI
kept_items.text: To keep pace with AI progress, we're advancing how we study Claude's economic impact, using hourly sampling and survey data.
kept_items.selection_reason: Anthropic's updated Economic Index with hourly sampling and first survey of Claude users. Data release, thread head, 2.1k likes. Replies unavailable for thread head; using 0, gap noted.

kept_items.author: AlexFinn
kept_items.text: Ornith-1.0 35b is the best local model I've run that doesn't require 200GB+ of RAM. Smarter and faster than Qwen 3.6 in my tests, runs well on a DGX Spark.
kept_items.selection_reason: Practitioner hands-on with the smaller Ornith-1.0 35b local model, claiming it beats Qwen 3.6 on a DGX Spark. 181k views.

kept_items.author: GergelyOrosz
kept_items.text: GLM-5.2 plus the US banning the most capable new models means open source caught up to SOTA closed source coding models. Could be problematic for Anthropic and OpenAI revenue and IPO plans.
kept_items.selection_reason: Sharp analytic take tying GLM-5.2 plus US frontier-model restrictions to a revenue/IPO risk for the closed labs. Credible practitioner voice, fresh (1h old).

kept_items.author: rileywestreel
kept_items.text: Amodei and Hassabis on when AGI lands: Amodei 1-2 years, Hassabis 5-10. Amodei: assume I'm right, why can't we slow down to Demis' timeline?
kept_items.selection_reason: Concrete on-stage exchange contrasting Amodei (AGI 1-2 yrs) and Hassabis (5-10 yrs), Amodei arguing for slowing to the longer timeline. Notable framing of the timeline debate.

kept_items.author: AnatoliKopadze
kept_items.text: Anthropic CEO: there are jobs that took generations to build that may disappear. The economy splits into people who use AI and people who get displaced.
kept_items.selection_reason: Widely shared clip of an Amodei interview on AI's labour-market split and jobs that may disappear. 262k views; complements the Econ Index data from a human-impact angle.

kept_items.author: jmrphy
kept_items.text: After a week with beta testers, I believe we have the ticket to solving slop in LLM output. It's a tiny 14b model fine-tuned with a specific technical innovation.
kept_items.selection_reason: Practitioner claim of a fine-tuned 14b model targeting LLM slop after a week of beta testing. Concrete technical observation, healthy reply engagement.

kept_items.author: cryptorover
kept_items.text: Musk says AI demand is now so extreme that production shortages have become insane. Tim Cook says tech cost inflation is the worst he has seen in 40 years.
kept_items.selection_reason: Strong-engagement item relaying Musk on AI-driven production shortages and Tim Cook on 40-year-high tech cost inflation. Macro/supply angle on the AI buildout. 330k views.
